summary.headline: Indo Borax Q4 FY26 revenue rose 25.7% to Rs 63.01 crore and PAT rose 41.9% to Rs 14.53 crore, with new promoter Zenrock in control.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 operating revenue was Rs 63.01 crore (up 25.7% YoY), with EBITDA of Rs 12.82 crore (20.4% margin) and PAT of Rs 14.53 crore (21.5% margin). FY26 revenue was Rs 215.45 crore (up 22.9%), EBITDA was flat at Rs 44.16 crore, and PAT was Rs 50.27 crore (up from Rs 42.51 crore). Management said the company changed control in January 2026 with Zenrock Chemicals as new promoter, and a new leadership team took over. A special dividend of Rs 30 per share plus a final dividend of Rs 10 per share (total Rs 40) was declared after monetising non-core assets. Management guided to Rs 250-plus crore revenue next year and 20-35% growth, but gave no formal numeric guidance, and no dividend policy has yet been declared.

financial_highlights.change: +41.9% YoY vs Rs 10.24 crore; PAT margin +250 bps

segments.name: Boric Acid Technical
segments.commentary: About 85-90% of current business per CEO; roughly 15,000-plus tons in FY26. Capacity is 20,000 tpa nameplate but historically 15,000-16,000 tons output, and it is running at full utilisation.

segments.name: Boric Acid I.P. Grade
segments.commentary: About 900 tons in FY26. Realisation is 10-15% higher than technical grade, using the same equipment with tighter specifications. Management intends to expand its share.

segments.name: DOT (Disodium Octaborate Tetrahydrate)
segments.commentary: 980 tons in FY26 (about 600 tons two years ago), out of 6,000 tpa capacity, so utilisation is low. Target is about 1,500 tons next year. Realisation is about Rs 150/kg and the Indian market is about 8,500 tons.

segments.name: Boron Oxide
segments.commentary: 4,000 tpa capacity project under construction; first lot expected in three to four quarters. Management pegs realisation at 2-3x Boric Acid pricing (cited 2.5x).

segments.name: Other / traded products
segments.commentary: Borax Pentahydrate (mostly traded), Gypsum (by-product, largest by volume), and other products together about 400 tons in FY26 per the CEO.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of about Rs 250-plus crore from debottlenecking and higher DOT sales, subject to raw material pricing.
Management said it is 'definitely surpassing' Q4 numbers in Q1 FY27 (April), though it did not give figures.
Revenue growth guided at 20-35% (about Rs 40-60 crore increments), with EBITDA margin maintained at or above the current 20-21% level.
Boron Oxide first lot expected in three to four quarters; CAPEX to be completed within FY27 plus a few months.
Capex plans for the next year are still under discussion and will be shared after board approval; a stated dividend policy is being framed but not yet declared.
capex_capacity: Nameplate capacity is about 26,000 tpa: 20,000 tpa Boric Acid and 6,000 tpa DOT. Boron Oxide 4,000 tpa is a project under way.

Boric Acid effective output is about 15,000-16,000 tons versus 20,000 nameplate due to planned shutdowns and raw material gaps. Management aims to add 1,000-1,500 tons through debottlenecking and tighter shutdown planning.
Possible Boric Acid capacity expansion is under internal board debate, not yet approved.
Management says cash on hand is sufficient for the capex budgeted over the next two years.
demand_pricing: Indian Boric Acid market is about 40,000 tpa, projected to reach about 53,000 tons by 2030 (8% CAGR). Steel and refractory accounts for 55-60% of demand. The company claims about 50% share.
Realisation was about Rs 127-128/kg in FY26 versus Rs 114-115/kg in FY25. EBITDA is about Rs 28-29/kg (20-21%) for Boric Acid.
Management said Boric Acid is sold out, and growth in value depends on price pass-through. Raw material costs rose sharply due to geopolitics, but management said pass-through has been achieved.
Raw material (boron ore/Ulexite) sourcing is concentrated in Turkey. The company is diversifying to South America and North America.
Top 10-15 customers have been stable for years, and management said the company has a premium price because of technical specifications, especially in steel refractories.

qa_highlights.question: Sales mix across Boric Acid Technical, I.P., DOT and Boron Oxide, and the EBITDA margin trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Boric Acid is about 90% of sales, DOT about 8%, others about 2%. Boric Acid EBITDA is about Rs 28-29/kg (20-21%), down from the 25-30% management said it earned in past years, and management said it expects to hold 20-22%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the peak revenue potential at full utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Without new capex, management said revenue could rise 25-30% over about 1.5 years, and up to 20-35% depending on raw material inflation and pricing. The base is about Rs 215 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Boron Oxide timeline and revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: First lot is expected in three to four quarters. Management said realisation is 2-3x Boric Acid, so it used 2.5x in its estimate.

qa_highlights.question: How did the new promoter's team (Zenrock) and the special dividend fit with reinvestment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cash was not fully distributed and enough remains for two years of budgeted capex. The dividend came from selling non-core assets (flats, cars) and was a one-time payout shared with old shareholders.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue and EBITDA guidance for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 revenue could be Rs 250 crore-plus, with growth of 20-35% and EBITDA margins held at or above current levels. Absolute numbers were not given to a retail participant due to insider trading policy.

qa_highlights.question: Promoter pledge and debt (raised by one participant)?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the company has zero debt. A participant cited Rs 400 crore of debt, and management referred the query to its IR team without answering.

risks_watch: Raw material cost volatility (boron ore sourced largely from Turkey) and geopolitical pressure on margins. Management says about 2 quarters of hedged purchasing.
DOT utilisation is very low (980 tons of 6,000 tpa). Management gave no clear reason for the slow growth, and a participant questioned quality or customer issues.
Governance and disclosure: promoter shares reportedly 100% pledged (not answered), a conflicting debt claim of Rs 400 crore, and a board-approved dividend policy still pending.
Zenrock's operating background was questioned; management said Zenrock is a holding company and the operating team is led by industry professionals.
Boron Oxide, new product lines and I.P. grade ramp are still at exploratory or project stage; timing is uncertain.
summary.management_tone: Confident on near-term results and the Q1 run rate, but evasive on specifics: on new products, Boron Oxide applications, DOT growth history, capex size and pledge/debt questions, management deferred answers. Guidance came with heavy caveats on raw material pricing.
key_quotes: So, we are confident that we are in a good situation and a good chemical sector, where the entire value chain could pass on the price increases to the whole set of their customers.
We have no complaints to make, trust me. We are happy with our results in April.
We have zero debt in Indo Borax.

adds.what: 4,000 tpa Boron Oxide plant (project under construction)
Boric Acid debottlenecking adding 1,000-1,500 tons/yr effective output

growth.why: Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 20-35% (about Rs 250-plus crore), backed partly by a 4,000 tpa Boron Oxide plant due in three to four quarters, Boric Acid debottlenecking of 1,000-1,500 tons, and DOT volume rising to about 1,500 tons from 980 tons on 6,000 tpa capacity, though no numeric order book or contracts were given and the Boric Acid expansion is still under board debate.

mgmt.note: Zenrock Chemicals took control as new promoter in January 2026 and a new leadership team took over; they guided to 20-35% revenue growth and a Rs 250-plus crore FY27 target, with DOT volume rising to about 1,500 tons and a 4,000 tpa Boron Oxide plant under construction.
